name_en: Satsuma ebi zoni — New Year mochi soup topped with a shrimp bigger than the bowl
summary_ja: 椀からはみ出すほど大きな焼きエビをのせた正月の雑煮。出水沖で伝統漁法によって獲られたエビを炭火で焼き、島津家に献上していた名残と伝わり、薩摩地域では冬の風物詩として軒先に焼きエビが吊るされる。
summary_en: A New Year mochi soup topped with a grilled shrimp so large it hangs over the bowl's rim. It's said to descend from shrimp caught off Izumi by traditional net-fishing, charcoal-grilled and once presented to the Shimazu clan; grilled shrimp still hang outside dried-goods shops there each winter.
source_title: さつまえび雑煮 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Satsuma jiru — a chicken-and-vegetable miso soup rooted in cockfighting tradition
summary_ja: 鶏肉やごぼう、里芋を煮こんだ具だくさんの味噌汁。薩摩武士が士風高揚のためおこなった闘鶏で、負けた鶏をその場でしめて野菜と煮たのが始まりと伝わり、鶏をよく食べる鹿児島の食文化を今に伝える。
summary_en: A hearty miso soup thick with chicken, burdock, and taro. It's said to trace back to Satsuma-domain cockfighting, where the losing bird was slaughtered on the spot and simmered with vegetables by the samurai who kept it — an early mark of Kagoshima's enduring taste for chicken.
source_title: さつま汁 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Mizuika no mada jiru — miso soup thickened black with squid ink and its liver sac
summary_ja: アオリイカ（ミズイカ）の身と墨袋（マダ）を味噌汁に溶き入れる奄美地域の汁物。イカ墨のまろやかな甘みとコクが持ち味で、マダはのぼせや血圧を下げる薬としても買い求められてきたという。
summary_en: A miso soup from Amami where bigfin reef squid meat and its ink sac are stirred straight into the broth. The ink lends a mellow sweetness and depth, and the sac itself has long been bought as a remedy said to ease flushing and high blood pressure.
source_title: ミズイカのマダ汁 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Buta hone yasai — bone-in pork and island vegetables simmered for New Year's Eve
summary_ja: 大きく切った骨付き豚肉とツワブキ、大根、里芋の在来種コシャマンを大鍋で煮こむ、奄美地域の大晦日に欠かせない料理。別名ウァンフィネヤッセといい、島豚を余さず食べ尽くす知恵の一皿とされる。
summary_en: Bone-in pork cut into big chunks is simmered in a large pot with tsuwabuki, daikon, and koshaman taro — an Amami dish essential to New Year's Eve, also called wanfineyasse. It's regarded as a wisdom born of using every part of the island's own black pigs.
source_title: 豚骨野菜 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Hechima jiru — young loofah simmered in barley miso, ladled over a bowl of somen
summary_ja: 若いへちまを麦味噌の汁で煮て、ゆでたそうめんにかけて食べる鹿児島の夏の料理。とろりとした食感と自然な甘みが麦味噌の甘さと重なり、お盆の精進料理としても欠かせない一椀である。
summary_en: Young loofah is simmered in a barley-miso broth and ladled over boiled somen — a Kagoshima summer dish. Its silky texture and natural sweetness echo the miso's own sweetness, and the bowl also has a place in the vegetarian dishes served at Obon.
source_title: へちま汁 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Buta jiru — pork and root vegetables in a sweet, low-salt barley-miso broth
summary_ja: 豚肉と大根、里芋などを煮こむ味噌汁で、飼育頭数の多い鹿児島の豚と、麹が多く甘みの強い麦味噌を合わせてつくる。冬に体を温める一椀として、家庭でも給食でも広く親しまれている。
summary_en: Pork simmered with daikon, taro, and other roots in a miso broth, built on Kagoshima's own pork — the prefecture raises more hogs than any other — paired with a barley miso high in koji and correspondingly sweet. A warming bowl for winter, common at home and in school lunches alike.
source_title: 豚汁 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理
